hero_kpi_rationale: Net sales remain the primary performance indicator for the company, reflecting overall commercial dynamics in a mature sector facing volume and mix challenges despite price increases.
company_description: The Kraft Heinz Company, together with its subsidiaries, manufactures and markets food and beverage products in North America and internationally. Its products include condiments, sauces, dressings, and spreads; cheese, frozen potato products, and other frozen meals; meal kits, frozen snacks, and pickles; dry packaged desserts, refrigerated ready to eat desserts, and other dessert toppings; ready to drink and powdered beverages, and liquid concentrates; American sliced and recipe cheeses; mainstream coffee, coffee pods, and premium coffee; and cold cuts, bacon, and hot dogs. It offers its products under the Kraft, Oscar Mayer, Heinz, Philadelphia, Lunchables, Velveeta, Ore-Ida, Capri Sun, Maxwell House, Kool-Aid, Jell-O, ABC, Master, Quero, Golden Circle, Wattie's, Pudliszki, and Plasmon brands, as well as Bagel Bites, Claussen, A1, and Cool Whip. kpis.name: Net Sales
kpis.explanation: Total sales after deducting returns and allowances.
kpis.description: Net sales decreased by 3.5% in 2025 compared to 2024, primarily due to unfavorable volume/mix (-4.1 pp), partially offset by price increases (+0.7 pp).
kpis.signal: Sales decline driven by volume/mix weakness despite price increases.

kpis.name: Operating Income
kpis.description: Operating income was -$4.7B in 2025 compared to +$1.7B in 2024, impacted by asset impairments (goodwill and intangible assets) totaling $9.3B.
kpis.signal: Major operating loss in 2025 due to asset impairments.

kpis.name: Gross Margin
kpis.explanation: Difference between sales and cost of goods sold, expressed as a percentage.
kpis.description: Gross margin remained stable at approximately 33.5% in 2025, supported by efficiency measures and pricing adjustments, despite inflationary pressures on the supply chain.
kpis.signal: Stable gross margin despite cost inflation.

kpis.name: Impairment Losses
kpis.explanation: Amount lost on assets that have declined in book value.
kpis.description: Total impairment losses of $9.3B in 2025 ($6.7B on goodwill, $2.6B on intangible assets), compared to $3.6B in 2024.
kpis.signal: Massive impairments in 2025 significantly impacting results.

kpis.name: Organic Net Sales
kpis.explanation: Net sales adjusted for foreign exchange, acquisitions, and divestitures.
kpis.description: Organic net sales declined by 3.4% in 2025, indicating a contraction in core business activity despite price increases.
kpis.signal: Organic decline reflecting weak demand or market share loss.

kpis.name: Divestitures
kpis.explanation: Proceeds from the sale of businesses or subsidiaries.
kpis.description: Divestiture of infant and specialty nutrition business in Italy for $146 million in December 2025.
kpis.signal: Portfolio reduction in Italy to refocus strategy.

kpis.name: Net Income
kpis.description: Net income extracted from SEC EDGAR companyfacts XBRL over the last eight reported fiscal years (10-K).
kpis.signal: Net income of -$5.846B in the latest fiscal year (FY2025).

kpis.name: Diluted EPS
kpis.description: Diluted EPS extracted from SEC EDGAR companyfacts XBRL over the last eight reported fiscal years (10-K).
kpis.signal: Diluted EPS of -$4.93 in the latest fiscal year (FY2025).

kpis.name: Dividends Per Share
kpis.description: Annual dividends per share paid, aggregated from yfinance.dividends over the last seven reported fiscal years.
kpis.signal: Dividends per share of $0.40 in the latest year.

kpis.name: Capital Returned (Dividends)
kpis.description: Capital returned to shareholders via annual dividends, extracted from yfinance.cashflow over the last four reported fiscal years.
kpis.signal: Capital returned to shareholders via dividends of $1.898B in the latest year.

kpis.name: Payout Ratio
kpis.description: Payout Ratio = Dividends Paid / Net Income, calculated over the last three fiscal years from yfinance.cashflow and yfinance.income_stmt.
kpis.signal: Portion of net income distributed as dividends: 70.4% in the latest year.

kpis.name: Removal of FD&C Colors
kpis.explanation: Commitment to remove artificial colors by end of 2027 in the United States.
kpis.description: Commitment announced in 2025 to remove all FD&C artificial colors from new products and the U.S. portfolio by end of 2027, primarily impacting Hydration and Desserts platforms.
kpis.signal: Portfolio transformation to align with health preferences.

kpis.name: SNAP Program Impact
kpis.explanation: Changes in U.S. food assistance programs affecting demand.
kpis.description: Modifications to the SNAP program in 2025 could reduce demand for Kraft Heinz products, which target lower-income consumers.
kpis.signal: Regulatory risk weighing on demand for affordable products.

kpis.name: Earnings Per Share
kpis.explanation: Net income divided by the weighted average number of diluted shares outstanding during the fiscal year. Measures the company's ability to generate earnings per share: used as the basis for the Payout Ratio (DPS / EPS).
kpis.description: 5-year history (2021-2025). Source: yfinance income statement (Diluted EPS).

risks.title: Intense competition and pricing pressure
risks.summary: The food industry is highly competitive, forcing the company to adjust prices and increase marketing expenses, which may reduce profitability.
risks.score_rationale: This risk is mentioned at the beginning of the 'Industry Risks' section and described as 'highly competitive'. The company emphasizes the need to lower prices or increase marketing spending to remain competitive, directly impacting profitability.

risks.title: Rapidly changing consumer preferences
risks.summary: The company must continuously anticipate and adapt to fast-changing consumer tastes, particularly around health and wellness, or risk losing market share.
risks.score_rationale: This risk is detailed in the 'Industry Risks' section, with the company stressing the need to predict and adapt to rapidly changing consumer tastes and habits, including health and wellness trends.

risks.title: Dependence on and power of large retailers
risks.summary: The consolidation of large retailers gives them increased bargaining power, potentially leading to pricing pressure and less favorable commercial terms for the company.
risks.score_rationale: This risk is clearly identified in the section addressing changes in the retail landscape. Retailer consolidation grants them greater negotiating power, affecting pricing and commercial terms.

risks.title: Product recall and liability risks
risks.summary: Product recalls due to contamination, labeling errors, or safety issues can result in significant financial losses and severely damage the company's reputation.
risks.score_rationale: This risk is presented as having a 'materially adversely affect' impact and is detailed with examples such as contamination, incorrect labeling, or undeclared allergens.

risks.title: Damage to reputation and brand image
risks.summary: Negative publicity, quality issues, environmental or social concerns, or the spread of misinformation can severely harm reputation and consumer trust.
risks.score_rationale: This risk is central in the section dedicated to reputation. It covers negative perceptions related to products, marketing practices, environmental or social issues, and the rapid spread of information (including false information) on social media.

risks.title: Failure in innovation and new product development
risks.summary: The inability to successfully develop and launch innovative new products or adapt to competitors' technological advances may harm market position and sales.
risks.score_rationale: This risk is linked to the company's ability to innovate and introduce new products, mentioned in the sections on competition and consumer preferences. Failure could impact sales and competitive positioning.

ai_positioning.summary: The company KHC does not mention artificial intelligence or machine learning in its 10-K/20-F report.
